proposal.reactor_type: Two-stage coiled tubular reactor with in-line static mixers (T-mixer -> coil 1 -> T-mixer -> coil 2), fully liquid-phase, no gas headspace
proposal.tubing_material: PFA (chemically resistant to TBHP, H2SO4, NaBr, dioxane)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Total liquid channel volume divided by combined outlet flow rate (post-mixing), consistent with batch's reported 30 min total reaction time

streams.pump_role: Delivers morpholine to second mixer after aldehyde intermediate forms
Delivers benzyl alcohol, NaBr, and H2SO4 to first mixer
streams.contents: Benzyl alcohol, NaBr (10 mol%), H2SO4 (10 mol%)

streams.pump_role: Delivers TBHP oxidant to first mixer (initiates oxidation/bromination cycle)

proposal.mixer_type: Two sequential low-dead-volume PEEK T-mixers (0.5 mm bore) for staged reagent introduction
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Benzyl alcohol, NaBr, and H2SO4 are combined with TBHP first (Stage 1) to generate the active hypobromite/bromide oxidant in situ and oxidize BnOH to benzaldehyde without premature amine oxidation. Morpholine is introduced only at the second mixer (Stage 2) so that it reacts with the pre-formed aldehyde to give the hemiaminal, which is then oxidized further by residual TBHP/NaBr to the amide. This mirrors the batch 'two-step' sequence and minimizes direct TBHP-amine side reactions (e.g., N-oxidation) that can occur if all reagents are mixed simultaneously.
pre_reactor_steps: Sparge all dioxane stock solutions with N2 to remove dissolved O2 (limits TBHP autodecomposition)
Pre-heat Stream B/C mixing zone to 70°C before entering Stage 1 coil
Pre-heat Stream A to 80°C before Stage 2 mixer to avoid thermal shock and maintain reaction temperature immediately upon amine addition
In-line filters (2 µm) on all pumps to prevent NaBr solid particulates from clogging micromixers
post_reactor_steps: In-line quench with saturated Na2S2O3 (aq) stream at reactor outlet to destroy excess TBHP
Cool to room temperature via post-reactor heat exchanger before BPR
Liquid-liquid separation (aqueous NaBr/H2SO4/thiosulfate salts vs. organic dioxane/product)
Concentrate organic phase and purify by silica chromatography or recrystallization to isolate benzoylmorpholine
proposal.chemistry_notes: Mechanism: NaBr is oxidized by TBHP to an electrophilic bromine species (Br+/hypobromite), which oxidizes benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde (Stage 1). Morpholine then condenses with benzaldehyde to form a hemiaminal (Stage 2), which is further oxidized by the TBHP/NaBr system to the tertiary amide (benzoylmorpholine). Sulfuric acid facilitates both alcohol activation and hemiaminal dehydration/oxidation steps. Excess TBHP (2.2 equiv) is required to drive both oxidation events to completion.

stage_1.purpose: Alcohol oxidation to aldehyde via NaBr/TBHP/H2SO4

stage_2.purpose: Amidative oxidation via hemiaminal intermediate to benzoylmorpholine

reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total 3.0 mL/min chosen to give a practical, lab-scale reactor volume (~90 mL) matching the 30 min total batch reaction time while keeping tubing length manageable (~50 m at 1.5 mm ID).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Derived directly from residence time × flow rate for each stage (10 min × 2.0 mL/min = 20→30 mL rounded for mixer dead volume; 20 min × 3.0 mL/min = 60 mL).
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Matches batch protocol's 0.667 M substrate concentration in dioxane; back-calculated stock concentrations assume equal-volume 3-stream mixing.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar back-pressure ensures single-phase liquid flow at 80°C (dioxane bp 101°C, but TBHP decomposition can generate O2/gaseous byproducts requiring pressurization to suppress bubble formation and maintain stable residence time).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.5 mm selected to balance reasonable coil length (~50 m) against mixing efficiency and pressure drop for a 90 mL total reactor volume.

literature_analogies: Continuous-flow NaBr/TBHP oxidative amidation protocols adapted from batch oxidative coupling methods (e.g., Maulide/Jiao-type TBHP/NaBr alcohol-to-amide couplings), translated to segmented-flow architecture to control reaction staging.

General flow chemistry precedent for staged oxidant/nucleophile addition to prevent nucleophile overoxidation (analogous to flow protocols for Swern/TEMPO/NaOCl oxidations coupled with in-line amidation).
safety_flags: TBHP is a peroxide oxidant; risk of exothermic decomposition and gas evolution — use dilute (≤4.4 M) TBHP stream, in-line pressure relief, and thermocouples with automatic shutoff at >100°C.
NaBr/H2SO4/TBHP combination may generate trace Br2 or HOBr; ensure fume hood/scrubber on reactor outlet.
Concentrated H2SO4 stream requires corrosion-resistant pump heads (PTFE/ceramic).
Post-reactor thiosulfate quench essential to prevent peroxide accumulation in waste stream.
All dioxane streams must be handled under inert atmosphere; dioxane is a peroxide-forming solvent and flammable (flash point 12°C).
proposal.confidence: medium – core stoichiometry and staged mixing rationale are consistent with known NaBr/TBHP oxidative amidation chemistry, but exact intermediate stage temperatures and residence-time split are inferred assumptions since the original batch report only specifies overall 80°C/30 min conditions.
